name: Suitability Obligation
description: A broker-dealer or associated person must have a reasonable basis to believe that a recommended transaction or investment strategy involving a security is suitable for the customer, based on the customer's investment profile, financial situation, and risk tolerance.

name: Communications with the Public
description: All member communications must be fair, balanced, and not misleading. Communications must not contain false, exaggerated, unwarranted, promissory or misleading statements or claims, nor omit any material fact.

name: Prohibition of Fraud and Insider Information
description: Unlawful to employ any device, scheme, or artifice to defraud, make untrue statements of material fact, or omit material facts necessary in connection with the purchase or sale of any security.

name: Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices
description: Prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices in offering or providing a financial product or service. Disclosures regarding interest rates, penalties, and recurring fees must be clear and conspicuous.

name: Customer Identification Program & AML
description: Financial institutions must implement reasonable procedures to verify the identity of any person opening an account, maintain records of the information used to verify identification, and monitor for suspicious transactions.

name: Internal Controls Over Financial Reporting
description: Requires management and the independent auditor to report on the adequacy of the company's internal control over financial reporting, prohibiting unauthorized alterations of accounting ledgers.

name: Customer Financial Information Safeguards
description: Financial institutions must ensure the security and confidentiality of customer information, protect against anticipated threats or unauthorized access to nonpublic personal information (NPI).

name: Best Execution Obligation
description: Investment firms must take all sufficient steps to obtain the best possible result for their clients when executing orders, taking into account price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement.
